proposed_comments.title: Clamp the preview-size setting at the settings boundary and preserve compatibility
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/peek/Peek.Settings/PreviewSizeSettings.cs` — `PreviewSizeSettings.Load` and `PreviewSizeSettings.ClampMaxPreviewSize`
- `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/Settings/PreviewSizeControl.xaml` — `MaximumPreviewSize` and the `NumberBox` binding

**Problem:** The new preview-size setting validates only when it is converted for display, not when it is restored from persisted settings. A hand-edited or older settings file can therefore reintroduce an out-of-range value and bypass the intended UI bounds.

**Why it matters:** Persisted values should be rejected or clamped at the settings boundary before they reach the renderer, or the user can silently get an invalid configuration that undermines the intended preview-size contract and accessibility label.

**Suggested change:**
1. Clamp or reject the restored `MaximumPreviewSize` value in the settings load path before it is exposed to the view model.
2. Preserve the legacy/default settings contract by keeping the 10 MB default when the saved value is missing or invalid and add round-trip coverage for older settings files.
3. Keep the `NumberBox` accessible name aligned with the existing preview-size header and add a regression test covering invalid persisted values.

**Verification:** Run the Peek settings and unit tests, then confirm an older or invalid saved value reloads to the clamped default and the `NumberBox` still exposes the correct label.

proposed_comments.title: Keep the bounded decoding and fallback path faithful to the text/binary contract
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/peek/Peek.FilePreviewer/PeekFileDecoder.cs` — `TryReadWithEncodingDetection` and `TryDetectEncoding`
- `src/modules/peek/Peek.FilePreviewer/PreviewFactory.cs` — `CreatePreviewForFile`

**Problem:** The bounded read path still depends on a short prefix for charset detection, so legacy encodings that only become distinguishable later can decode incorrectly. BOM-less UTF-16/UTF-32 text can also be rejected when NUL-containing content is treated as binary too early, and the implementation comment still implies a constant-memory path instead of the actual buffered-result behavior.

**Why it matters:** Valid text can be misclassified as binary or rendered with corrupted characters, and the documented memory contract becomes inaccurate to the actual buffered-decoding pipeline.

**Suggested change:**
1. Sample beyond a short prefix when detecting encoding, and only classify NUL-heavy content as binary after BOM-less UTF-16/UTF-32 and other plausible text cases are rejected.
2. Keep the preview factory deterministic for text, binary, and oversized files by asserting the same fallback path for each case and covering the end-to-end regression tests.
3. Update the decoder comment to describe the bounded read plus buffered decoded-result behavior instead of claiming constant-memory rendering.

**Verification:** Run the Peek file-previewer unit tests and fallback regression coverage; verify a legacy-encoded sample, BOM-less UTF-16/UTF-32 sample, and oversized binary sample each follow the expected path.
